Correct under the supplied accepted internal inputs. The proposition, corollary and analytic example were checked in textual order, with 17 detailed statement checks and seven reference/inventory checks persisted.

Both strict-domination applications have the correct signs and hypotheses. For monotonicity, use a=u_psi, b=u_phi+t and r=c_psi/c_phi<1 under the contradiction assumption. For the lower comparison, use a=u_phi, b=h+t and r=c_phi/((1-epsilon)^n c_0)<1. Bounded equivalence transfers the smaller-background condition to each first potential; the required ordinary order holds for each second potential. Arbitrary translations contradict the conclusions at a common finite point. Finite-level positivity gives the factor (1-epsilon)^n, hence exactly n log(1-epsilon) after taking logarithms. Exhaustion off the smooth-volume-null pole set justifies the density bound without subtracting infinite measures. Taking defining suprema gives both dual bounds, including infinite values.

The estimate sup over all G in C(X) of |B_phi_j(G)-B_0(G)| <= delta_j, where delta_j=-n log(1-epsilon_j), proves uniform convergence on the entire unbounded Banach space. The supporting identity and dual comparison give a finite dual-minimization error between zero and delta_j. All probabilities lie in the single finite H_0 sublevel with level B_0(0)+2M+sup_j delta_j. Lower semicontinuity, convergence of the varying test integrals and continuity of B_0 imply that every weak cluster point minimizes the zero-reference dual problem. The accepted sublevel theorem supplies uniform integrability and weak L1 convergence. Compactness gives whole-sequence convergence when A_0(G) is a singleton.

For the analytic example, semipositivity makes ta both theta-psh and t theta-psh. The analytic-envelope theorem gives phi_t equivalent to ta; bounded-change invariance then proves P_theta[phi_t]=phi_t. Since ta<=phi_t, it supplies a genuine competitor for P_(t theta)(phi_t). Thus the comparison applies with epsilon=t. For Hermitian theta and fixed smooth G, Gauduchon recovery identifies the unique limiting supporting probability and yields weak L1 convergence of every selection.

No BMP/PVP, potential uniqueness, general ordinary-envelope idempotence, strong L1 convergence, additional mass property or arbitrary-reference convergence is used. The stated chapter placement avoids circularity. All invoked references are accepted internal inputs; no external-paper citation required search. Manuscript files, prior reports, frozen inputs, source references and Git publication were left untouched.
